text: Deadlines are a part of everyday life, but handling them well takes practice. The first step is good time management: break a large task into smaller, manageable pieces and set mini-deadlines for each one. Next, learn to prioritize. Not everything is equally urgent, so focus on the most important tasks first and be willing to say no to less critical requests. Scope management is also key. If a project keeps growing, gently push back and clarify what is actually required. Finally, communicate early and often. If you see a problem coming, tell your team or boss right away—it is much easier to adjust a plan than to explain a missed deadline.
